bug_semantics: The local stdio MCP tool get_smadex_report accepts caller-controlled downloadUrl with only z.string() validation, passes it unchanged through downloadReport(downloadUrl) to node-fetch fetch(url), follows the resulting outbound request, reads the response body, and returns that body to the caller. With no scheme, hostname, resolved-address, port, redirect, or network-boundary policy, an MCP caller can make the server process request loopback, private, link-local, metadata, or attacker-selected destinations and read the response, producing full-read SSRF from the server's network context.
flaw_origin: Commit aaff3decbc880724bbbe30810a50aa1ac42359c5 added the new Smadex MCP package and, in src/smadex-reporting/src/index.ts, simultaneously introduced both ends of the vulnerable path: the get_smadex_report tool's unrestricted downloadUrl: z.string() input and downloadReport's direct const response = await fetch(url) sink. The implementation included no destination validation before the request and no redirect revalidation.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object identifies both author and committer as steven <wuqi0509@gmail.com>; its complete message is "Add smadex mcp" and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, assistant, or bot trailer, while neither commit-object identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party report https://github.com/feed-mob/fm-mcp-servers/issues/198 is still open and documents the exact source-to-sink path in version 0.0.3: attacker-controlled downloadUrl is only z.string(), reaches downloadReport(downloadUrl), then fetch(url), and the response text is returned; its localhost PoC confirms the outbound request. GitHub advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fhw4-v2hr-j5m2 maps this report to CVE-2026-19770 / GHSA-fhw4-v2hr-j5m2, names src/smadex-reporting/src/index.ts:downloadReport, lists affected and patched versions as unknown, and states that the project had not responded.

git log HEAD --full-history -p -L '/^async function downloadReport/,/^}/':src/smadex-reporting/src/index.ts traces the complete vulnerable function, including const response = await fetch(url), to the single non-merge commit aaff3decbc880724bbbe30810a50aa1ac42359c5 ("Add smadex mcp"). The BIC diff creates src/smadex-reporting/src/index.ts from /dev/null and also creates the get_smadex_report tool with downloadUrl: z.string() and the direct call downloadReport(downloadUrl). Merge b83bee4db45338a492c03d40fd96b184db879f26 later integrated the branch, so the merge is not the smallest BIC; there is no squash to decompose.

Direct-parent verification: the BIC commit object names sole parent ab4179e9ad97966db18119c3700f69dc849cd760, and git ls-tree -r --name-only ab4179e9ad97966db18119c3700f69dc849cd760 -- src/smadex-reporting returns no paths. Thus the package, tool source, unrestricted input, and fetch sink are absent from the immediate parent tree rather than merely renamed or moved.

Affected-version boundary: aaff3decbc880724bbbe30810a50aa1ac42359c5 introduced package version 0.0.1; cd8b313b4154a7492074ad9b1e1bacdafa3d5e98 bumped it to 0.0.2; 51ed50a5eb7f0235f1d32285852c9634f9092caf bumped it to 0.0.3. The -L history shows no intervening change to downloadReport. The npm registry at https://registry.npmjs.org/%40feedmob%2Fsmadex-reporting lists exactly 0.0.1, 0.0.2, and 0.0.3, with 0.0.3 latest; its recorded gitHeads b83bee4db45338a492c03d40fd96b184db879f26, 699e17b5b0d5f4c8cdff38e09b7a5c5cda1d0472, and e203cce8ba7145806ecb971173110ceea783920d all contain the BIC by git merge-base --is-ancestor. Therefore every published version 0.0.1 through 0.0.3 contains the flawed mechanism, including the advisory's named 0.0.3.

Fix and patched-boundary check: git log --all --full-history -- src/smadex-reporting/src/index.ts has no source change after merge e203cce8ba7145806ecb971173110ceea783920d, local main HEAD 3024176fc3996d7e023732dc968b9c4d036b2d70 still contains z.string(), downloadReport(downloadUrl), and fetch(url), and current upstream source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/feed-mob/fm-mcp-servers/main/src/smadex-reporting/src/index.ts is identical at that path. Published 0.0.3 source at https://unpkg.com/@feedmob/smadex-reporting@0.0.3/dist/index.js retains the unrestricted fetch and is still npm latest. No fix commit, direct fix member, or patched release exists in the available public history, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are null because the vulnerability is unpatched.

BIC-only AI attribution: numactl-prefixed git cat-file -p aaff3decbc880724bbbe30810a50aa1ac42359c5 shows author steven <wuqi0509@gmail.com>, committer steven <wuqi0509@gmail.com>, and only the message "Add smadex mcp" after the signed headers. There is no AI co-author/generation trailer or bot identity on the commit object; later branch names, PR metadata, or unrelated commits were not used for attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerability is causal, not merely a suspicious API call: a caller-controlled MCP argument crosses no semantic URL or destination check, reaches node-fetch in the server's network context, and the fetched body is returned. Line history identifies aaff3decbc880724bbbe30810a50aa1ac42359c5 as the smallest source commit that first wrote the complete Smadex-specific mechanism; its direct parent has no src/smadex-reporting tree, and the later merge is only integration. The BIC predates and is ancestral to all three published package versions, whose vulnerable function remained unchanged. Public main and npm latest remain vulnerable after the open report, making this a genuinely unpatched case with no fix boundary to name. Finally, the only allowed attribution evidence—the BIC commit object—contains a human author/committer and no AI marker, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched as of 2026-08-28: no public fix commit, direct fix member, or patched package version exists, so a fix SHA and patched-version boundary cannot be supplied; this is the explicit unpatched exception rather than an unresolved BIC or attribution gap.

unpatched.reason: Unpatched as of 2026-08-28: no public fix commit, direct fix member, or patched package version exists; this is the explicit unpatched state rather than an unresolved BIC or attribution gap.

potential_fix.approach: Validate downloadUrl against an allowlist (https scheme, public host), resolve DNS and reject private/loopback/link-local addresses, and require confirmation for arbitrary remote downloads in the stdio tool.
potential_fix.rationale: Constraining the URL channel at the tool boundary blocks SSRF and unintended local-file retrieval through downloadReport.
